newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ambles higher in light, routine trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ambles higher in light, routine trade.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ambled slightly higher by Friday midsession but traders said the activity was light and centred on routine trades.
July stood two stg up at 990 stg a tonne by the morning close after ranging between 988 and 995.
Technically, the April 9 low of 980 stg remained a significant support. A break below that level could trigger more losses.
Cocoa dipped below the 1,000 stg mark for the first time this week since April 10 as speculators unloaded cocoa on a perception of mounting supplies.
Traders said there was some light industry interest this morning in reaction to an early slide in sterling against against mark and dollar.
But by mid-morning sterling recouped some losses.
Traders called New York to open unchanged to $5 down.
New York's July cocoa closed $9 down at $1,391 a tonne and traders said a fall to below $1,380 could trigger some light sell-stops.
Broker GNI said clearly the action of the past few days reflected the market's acceptance that supplies from Ivory Coast would be better than previously expected.
It also said the International Cocoa Organisation's revised production deficit estimate of 115,000 tonnes for 1996/97, down from its earlier estimate 225,000 tonnes, was still seen as too high.
On Wednesday, GNI estimated the deficit at 33,000 tonnes.
